question: One of our specs has tests with the IDs `login`, `user-login-sso`, `LoginPage`, and `signup`. For a quick CI smoke job I want to run only `login` and `signup`. `npx doc-detective -i docs -t login -t signup` exits 2 with an error, and `-t login` by itself also runs `user-login-sso` and `LoginPage`. What's the right command?

facts.text: Each `--test` pattern is a case-insensitive regular expression that matches anywhere in the `testId`, so `login` also matches `user-login-sso` and `LoginPage`; anchor it as `^login$` to match only that ID.
`--test` takes one comma-separated list given once; repeating the flag is a usage error that exits 2.
The command is `npx doc-detective -i docs --test '^login$,^signup$'` (or the single pattern `'^(login|signup)$'`), quoted so the shell leaves the `$` and `|` alone.

must_not: `--test` matches the whole test ID exactly, or only from the start of the ID, or case-sensitively.
Separate the patterns with spaces, as in `-t login signup`.

wrong.answer:
`--test` compares the whole test ID, so `login` should only match `login`. The 2 exit comes from quoting. Repeat the flag once per test, with each ID quoted:

```bash
npx doc-detective -i docs -t "login" -t "signup"
```

Give `--test` once, as a comma-separated list. Repeating the flag exits `2`.

```bash
npx doc-detective -i docs --test login,signup
```
